text: Digital button -> key is exact: synthetic BTN_SOUTH -> JSM 'S' -> KEY_SPACE at evdev, ~2 ms latency, exact press/release count and order.
Digital button -> key is exact on Steam Input: clean press/release pairs at XI2, pipeline ~34 ms stimulus-to-raw-emission.

Tap/hold ('E = A B'): short press (<HOLD_PRESS_TIME) fires tap binding on release; long press fires hold binding AT threshold and suppresses tap. HOLD_PRESS_TIME is GLOBAL — one value governs every binding at once (audit gotcha X.2 confirmed); JSM has no per-binding hold time.

JSM tap/hold wall-clock boundary = HOLD_PRESS_TIME + up to ~1 poll tick (~8-16 ms slack): at 150 ms setting, 150 and 155 ms presses still TAP; hold fires by 170 ms. Threshold is logical/exclusive-ish; per-ms-exact translation is bounded_approximation.

Steam Long Press Time is PER-BINDING (450 ms default and custom 603 ms honored simultaneously in one layout) and inclusive/tick-exact at the configured value: 430 ms -> tap, 450 and 470 ms -> hold at setting 450. Long press suppresses the regular binding (interruptable default).

vdf 'interruptable' is a per-activator flag, default ON, and lives on the activator being INTERRUPTED (Full_Press/Regular — first attempt on the Long_Press activator changed nothing). With interruptable 0, Regular fires on press-down and is NOT suppressed when Long fires at threshold (both keys active together). Load-bearing for tap/hold translation; never assume default.
JSM double press ('N=B', 'N,N=X'): the FIRST press fires the base binding immediately, the second fires the double binding — base echo always present.
DBL_PRESS_WINDOW is measured first-RELEASE-to-second-DOWN — proven by construction (two probes, identical 200 ms down-to-down gaps, different hold times, different outcomes).

Steam Double Tap Time epoch is DOWN-TO-DOWN (oracle-attested, trace-consistent: 170 ms d2d fires double, 190 ms d2d at DTT=190 fired single, release-to-down ruled out by measurement). Boundary-EDGE inclusivity is UNRESOLVED and ruled MOOT under the human-food tolerance doctrine (~10-15 ms practical equality); the epoch itself stays product-relevant (divergence scales with hold duration).

Steam SUPPRESSES the base binding on a double-bound button and delays every single: suppressed single fires at first-down + DTT exactly (TRACE-PINNED: N=14 over 50-750 ms holds, F3 raw press at 192.23 +/- 0.84 ms from first-down at DTT=190; pipeline 33.84 +/- 0.44 ms); double fires immediately on second down (~0 ms added, 5 true doubles); held-double emits exactly one down at second-down and one up at second-up — nothing at first-down+DTT (re-send axiom falsified). Quick-tap suppressed single emits as a ~34 ms raw tap; held past DTT the raw key mirrors button state.

Activator timers anchor to DOWN-event timestamps (oracle axiom, now trace-pinned via batch-1 predictions 1-3). The retracted second clause (held action re-sent continuously) is FALSIFIED: a held Steam binding is one key-down -> held state -> one key-up; no re-send chatter, no inherent repeat.

Chorded press ('L=NONE', 'W=B', 'L,W=G'): W alone -> B; W while L held -> G — the chord overrides the owner's base binding. Modifier was bound NONE in this trace, so JSM member-leak behavior (modifier with its own binding active during chord) is UNTESTED.

Steam chord: owner's regular binding suppressed when the chord fires, but the chord MEMBER'S own binding LEAKS (TL's Shift held down alongside the chord's Q). Docs make no member-suppression claim — leak is by-design, not a bug.

JSM simultaneous press has PERSISTENT sticky state: a lone chord-member press AFTER an L+R chord re-emits the chord binding (Q) instead of the lone binding; gaps of 100/300/1000 ms do not clear it — only JSM restart/reconnect does. Clean once, then sticky -> degraded_approximation for any layout reusing a chord member as a lone button. Classified, not patched (non-semantic boundary).

ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS (source review, NOT runtime-confirmed): JoyShock::getMatchingSimBtn matches by pure state-equality (button1->getState() == button2->getState()), not 'both in WaitSim' — author flagged the flaw inline. A chord member not settled back to NoPress can re-pair with a new presser. Confirm via DEBUG_LOG of both buttons' states across the second lone press.

Steam has NO simultaneous-press primitive — only chords owned by one button. Lone-press-after-chord emits the lone binding correctly on Steam (verified both orders); the JSM sticky-state bug has no Steam counterpart.

JSM ZR/ZRF (NO_SKIP) fires off the analog ABS_RZ axis threshold, not a digital latch: soft pull -> soft binding; full pull adds full binding while keeping soft; an instant 0->255 single-event jump fires soft+full ~3 ms apart (any crossing counts).

Steam trigger edge(soft)+click(full) under a STAGED pull approximates JSM NO_SKIP (soft stays held while full active) — but an instant 0->255 jump emits FULL ONLY (no soft). Structural cross-runtime delta, confirmed on consistent evidence across sessions.

Steam soft-pull threshold is ADAPTIVE STATE, not a constant: fresh client, staged RZ=100 does NOT fire soft (yet identical stimulus verifiably fired it in Phase 2 after heavy trigger use); RZ=200 fires soft+full reliably; one crossing does not recalibrate within-session. Attribution to 'adaptive_threshold 3' is an UNPROVEN hypothesis. Converter: soft-pull translations inherit threshold instability -> classify <= bounded_approximation with the caveat named.
LEFT_STICK_MODE=NO_MOUSE with LUP/LDOWN/LLEFT/LRIGHT: directional keys held while tilted past the inner deadzone — exact WASD-style stick-to-keys.
Steam stick dpad-mode (directional WASD held while past deadzone) matches JSM LEFT_STICK_MODE=NO_MOUSE semantics.

Start_Press fires on press-down in EVERY tested configuration: batch-1 marker (validated, instant ~34 ms raw tap) and all 16 matrix cells regardless of slot position or co-residents (matrix half is trace-single-pass).

Release_Press is SUPPRESSED in clean disk-loaded layouts whenever a state-bound (Long/Double) or Start co-resident is present: absent in ALL 16 matrix cells at every slot position 1st-4th (trace-single-pass, state not controlled). NOT slot-order-specific — the GUI-observed order effect did not reproduce; hidden state, not visible order, drives the GUI flip. Release_Press bound ALONE fires correctly (oracle GUI evidence). Expected emission signature when it does fire: a zero/near-zero-duration combined down/up raw pair at physical-release + pipeline (oracle mechanic, untraced).

Double_Press is FULLY suppressed under Start+Release co-residency (matrix Set B, all 6 permutations) — even on in-window double-taps (d2d ~120 ms < DTT=190). Contrast batch-1 marker (Regular+Double co-residency: double pinned at second-down). The activator-loss hazard zone is wider than edge-eating. Claim strength: trace-single-pass.

TERMINOLOGY (oracle correction, ground truth = user's GUI-produced autosave, 13 occurrences): 'Full_Press' is NOT a distinct activator type — it is Valve's vdf serialization key for the GUI's 'Regular Press'. GUI activator list: Regular/Start/Release/Long/Double/Chorded; 'Full' appears in the GUI only as the trigger full-pull INPUT. Run artifacts keep the vdf key; prose says Regular.

CONVERTER HAZARD RULE (doctrine, trace+oracle-backed): button configs mixing Start/Release Press with Long/Double Press are a hazard zone — state-dependent activator loss (a probable Steam Input bug; state-driver hunt DE-SCOPED per environment-trust doctrine). Conversions touching such combos classify <= degraded_approximation with the hazard named; NEVER convert INTO such a combo (anti-Goodhart). Rule absorbs residual uncertainty regardless of matrix outcome.

OBSERVATION-PLANE METHOD RULE: Steam Input emits at the XI2 RAW layer; raw timestamps are authoritative (pipeline ~34 ms). Key-layer (device) events are flush-on-next-raw-event queue artifacts; the final pending release is synthesized by xinput test-xi2 at client exit. ALL timing analysis and comparator input MUST use Raw* events only (normalizer enforces, commits f5655dd/4adeedf). Method doctrine — lives in findings, not canonical mapper semantics.

HYPOTHESIS (INFERRED, unpinned): the ~34 ms quick-tap raw width of suppressed singles plausibly equals cvar controller_min_activation_time = 0.0333 s. Could be pinned by varying the cvar via steam-console live. Do not promote or build on until pinned.

ANOMALY (method-relevant): on synthetic-pad destruction JSM emitted a lone BTN_RIGHT down (trigger axis re-read during SDL device removal). Normalizer should discard output bracketing connect/disconnect events.
